# Sherwin Carlquist Digital Extended Specimen Network: full content

> Public site for a BRIT/Fort Worth Botanic Garden and California Botanic Garden project (NSF Awards 2133562 and 2133561) that links the botanical specimens, field images, publications, and archival materials of Sherwin Carlquist (1930–2021). Site: https://britorg.github.io/carlquist_esn/ (concise index: llms.txt)

## About the project

Sherwin Carlquist (1930–2021) was one of the preeminent botanists of the twentieth century. His contributions to wood anatomy, island biogeography, and plant systematics span more than 340 publications over six decades. The network connects the physical and digital traces of his career (specimens, field photographs, published research, archival collections) held at the Botanical Research Institute of Texas (BRIT) and the California Botanic Garden, and makes them machine-readable through open standards and Wikidata.

The project is a collaboration between BRIT at the Fort Worth Botanic Garden (NSF Award 2133562, lead institution) and California Botanic Garden (NSF Award 2133561).

- Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherwin_Carlquist
- Wikidata: https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q2251003

## Collections

- Carlquist Collection at BRIT/FWBG: correspondence, reprints, field materials, and related archives. Overview: https://fwbg.org/carlquist
- Field images (digitized): Portal to Texas History, https://texashistory.unt.edu/explore/collections/SJCC/
- RSA Herbarium, California Botanic Garden: vascular plant specimens collected by Carlquist, particularly from Pacific islands and California. https://www.cch2.org/portal/collections/misc/collprofiles.php?collid=17
- RSA-Wood Xylarium, California Botanic Garden: wood specimens central to his comparative anatomy research. https://www.cch2.org/portal/collections/misc/collprofiles.php?collid=105

## Data and tools

- Extended Specimen Network diagram (https://britorg.github.io/carlquist_esn/extended_specimen.html): concentric rings show Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Extensions of a specimen. Diagram adapted from Thiers et al. (2019), "Extending U.S. Biodiversity Collections to Promote Research and Education".
  - Represented in the Carlquist ESN: Physical Specimens (RSA Herbarium, RSA Xylarium, Carlquist Collection at BRIT/FWBG); Digital Specimen Record and Specimen Media (via CCH2); Field Notes (notebooks and correspondence in the BRIT/FWBG collection); Field Images (Portal to Texas History); Descriptions, Traits, and Distributions (documented across the 343 publications).
  - Part of the broader framework but not represented: Isotope Samples, Morphometric Data (measurements appear in published wood-anatomy work but are not aggregated), Gene Sequences, Phylogenies (not aggregated, though his work informed phylogenetic study), Interactions, Protection Status & Locations.
- Publications dataset (one component of the network, covering publications only; it does not include specimens, media, field notes, field images, or archival materials): bibliographic metadata for all 343 known publications, 1956–2021, in CSL-JSON and Dublin Core, with lookup tables for journals and co-authors. CC0. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18687469 (repository: https://github.com/BRITorg/carlquist_publications_dataset)
- Publications Explorer (https://britorg.github.io/carlquist_esn/publications_explorer.html): interactive dashboard to filter by year, journal, type, or co-author, with charts and links to Wikidata items.
- Wikidata integration: all 343 publications are matched to or created as Wikidata items; person, publication, and journal items are interlinked and queryable via the Wikidata Query Service.

## Products

- The Sherwin Carlquist Website: https://britorg.github.io/carlquist_web/ (original: https://web.archive.org/web/20220525065400/http://www.sherwincarlquist.com/)
- Sincerely, Sherwin: online exhibit by California Botanic Garden. https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/75f901d150b24d21a6ce0b6cfcaa7913
